subject: Finalize invoice cadence, tax handling & min-commit appendix
messages:
From: Ben Sharp <ben.sharp@procurement.finco.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <billing@finco.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form questions: invoice cadence, tax, and min-commit appendix

Hi Sofia,

We reviewed the updated Order Form (attached) and have a few outstanding items before procurement can route for PO sign-off:

- Invoice cadence: Can Redwood invoice quarterly or does billing require monthly invoicing? Our AP team prefers quarterly statements for large committed spend.
- Net terms: The redline currently says Net 30; can you confirm ability to move to Net 45?
- Taxes: We need confirmation on who is responsible for sales/use VAT/withholding and whether you can accept our tax certificate.
- Minimum commit appendix: Procurement also asked for a clear definition of the minimum-commit calculation (proration, usage offsets, etc.).

I've attached the Order Form v2 and the FinCo tax certificate for reference. Can we get a short summary of proposed commercial language so we can finish legal review?

Thanks —
Ben Sharp
Senior Procurement Manager
FinCo Analytics

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ben Sharp <ben.sharp@procurement.finco.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <billing@finco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions: invoice cadence, tax, and min-commit appendix

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (Finance) and Aditya (Legal) — and Laura from Sales Ops — to propose final wording.

Plan from our side:
- Marcus will propose an invoice cadence option that supports quarterly statements with one consolidated invoice per quarter (with month-level breakout).
- We can evaluate Net 45; need finance approval and internal sign-off on collections cadence. Marcus, can you confirm?
- Aditya will review tax/responsibility language and confirm whether your tax certificate is sufficient; he may propose a standard "tax allocation" paragraph or an alternate gross-up phrase.
- I'll circulate a short appendix draft that defines minimum-commit calculations (proration on effective date, usage credits, rounding rules) for your procurement to review.

Would it help if we provided a redline of the Order Form + a single-page summary of the changes for your Legal/Procurement? Happy to get that to you by EOD tomorrow (PST).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced: FinCo_OrderForm_v2.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Sharp <ben.sharp@procurement.finco.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <billing@finco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order form questions: invoice cadence, tax, and min-commit appendix

Hi all — finance input below. Short answers first: quarterly invoicing = OK; Net 45 = possible but needs slight price adjustment (see note); tax handling = FinCo responsibility for indirect taxes where applicable, Redwood will provide tax invoices.

Details / proposed language (for insertion into Order Form):
- Invoice cadence: "Customer may elect quarterly consolidated invoicing. Redwood will issue one invoice per calendar quarter, with supporting monthly usage detail attached. Invoices are due per the Net Terms selected in this Order Form."
- Net terms: "Default: Net 30. Customer may request Net 45; if Net 45 is selected, Redwood reserves the right to apply a 0.5% financing surcharge on the quarterly invoice total to offset extended credit terms."
- Taxes: "All fees are exclusive of taxes. Customer is responsible for any sales, use, VAT, or withholding taxes arising from this Order Form, except for taxes based on Redwood's net income. Customer will provide valid tax exemption or certificate where appropriate; Redwood will accept the Tax Certificate dated 2026-10-28 provided it is in English and issued by an authorized FinCo representative."

I've attached the Tax_Certificate_FinCo.pdf and sketched a one-page summary for Ben and Elena. Laura — please advise on invoice delivery (email vs. EDI) and PO matching requirements so we can align the AR process.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: Tax_Certificate_FinCo.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Sharp <ben.sharp@procurement.finco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order form questions: invoice cadence, tax, and min-commit appendix

Thanks — I reviewed Marcus's proposed language and attached a tracked redline of the Order Form + a short appendix for minimum-commit mechanics (see RI_OrderForm_Appendix_MinCommit.docx and MSA_redlines_aditya.docx). Key legal points:

- Min-commit appendix: define "Minimum Commit" as the contracted committed spend for the period with proration on both ramp and termination. Include an example table showing prorated monthly amounts and the calculation for a mid-quarter termination.
- Invoice credits: include explicit process for applying usage-based credits against committed spend before invoicing any shortfall charge to Customer.
- Taxes: Clarify that Redwood collects taxes where required by law and that Customer is responsible for withholding obligations; include a representation from Customer that it will provide accurate tax forms and notify Redwood of changes in tax status within 30 days.
- Net terms / surcharge: if you accept the 0.5% surcharge for Net 45, add a clause that the surcharge is waived if payment is made within 60 days in the event of a documented dispute resolved in Customer's favor.

Ben — attached documents are for your review. If procurement wants alternate wording on tax responsibility (e.g., seller collects VAT) we can consider a jurisdiction-specific exhibit.

Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: RI_OrderForm_Appendix_MinCommit.docx, MSA_redlines_aditya.docx

From: Ben Sharp <ben.sharp@procurement.finco.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <billing@finco.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions: invoice cadence, tax, and min-commit appendix

Sofia / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix. Procurement and legal reviewed the redlines and we have two follow-ups: 

1) Net terms: our AP team prefers Net 45 and is willing to accept the 0.5% surcharge for extended terms, but asks that the surcharge be capped at 0.5% per quarter and not compounded on outstanding balances. Can you confirm?
2) Minimum-commit examples: the appendix is helpful — would you add one more example that shows a customer credit when usage exceeds commit (i.e., rollover credit vs. cash refund)?

If we can get confirmation on those two items and a final redline (clean + tracked), we can push this to PO issuance next week.

Best regards,
Ben

On a separate note — Elena, please confirm you can accept quarterly consolidated invoices via billing@finco.com and the PO number format is FINCO-YYYY-####.
